s_About-C.text:
What: Governance as a real reading experience — the bylaws are the official web text with a sticky contents rail, "In plain words" summaries, redlines that show exactly what each vote changed, a per-version change log…

Borrowed from: Chicago Councilmatic (searchable decisions, plain summaries, subscribe), Keep a Changelog (Added/Changed/Removed/Fixed per…

Trade-off: The secretary has to enter motions and section versions in a structured way after each meeting instead of uploading one PDF; if that slips, the register and change log go stale.

s_About-D.text:
What: A living heritage page — a Reigning champions band (the same data feeds a one-line homepage band), an honor roll filtered by title with "Show all N years" and player pages behind every name, a single timeline from Morphy's birth (1837) through LCA's 1915 start to Sulphur 2026 beside a step-through Opera Game board…

Borrowed from: North Carolina Chess Association and Irish Chess Union (current-champions band, filterable champions table by year and title…

Trade-off: Most of the value depends on someone digitising old records and moderating submissions; until the archive grows, many rows and timeline points stay as gaps (which the page shows openly rather than hiding).

s_Member-A.text:
What: Eligibility first. Two yes/no questions, then a household builder that prices every combination (Family vs Adult/Senior + Scholastic), recommends the cheapest and prints the family math openly ("Family only saves with three children"). All four tiers sit below with the fitting one highlighted.

Borrowed from: USA Pickleball and AMNH (separate Join and Renew paths, tiers described by who they cover), Patreon (one highlighted tier…

Trade-off: The questions add a step for people who already know they want Adult, so the plain tier cards must stay one click away. The optimizer's rules (ties, seniors, up to 3 children, adding a child later) must match board policy exactly…

s_Member-B.text:
What: A conventional, easy-to-scan pricing page built on honest numbers: four tier cards described by who they cover, one highlight with a label that is literally true ("Best value with 3 children") and the family math printed on the card.

Borrowed from: Patreon (single highlighted tier), AMNH and USA Pickleball (tiers by who's covered, Renew next to Join)…

Trade-off: Less guided than Member-A, so visitors still pick the tier themselves. The dues breakdown is only credible once the treasurer enters real figures. Auto-renew brings Stripe subscription upkeep (failed cards, cancellations, refunds).

s_Member-C.text:
What: A purpose-first /donate page. The donor picks one of three funds ("Send a Louisiana kid to Nationals", "Club equipment", "General fund"), each with its goal and progress, then fills a short sticky form: once or monthly, four amounts plus Other (numeric keypad), a board-approved impact line, cover-the-fee…

Borrowed from: GiveDirectly and Wikimedia (plain framing, amount buttons, a trust fact up front), NN/g nonprofit study (say where donations go…

Trade-off: Fund accounting is ongoing work. The treasurer must log spending per fund for the table and progress bars to stay true, an officer has to review sponsored-entry requests before each event…

s_Member-D.text:
What: One membership card in four places (Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes with front and back, a My LCA card with a pass per child, printable member and family cards) sharing one signed QR that checks people in at the director's table or by scanning the door poster; on event days the pass shows round, board and color.

Borrowed from: Apple Wallet pass layout (header/primary/secondary/auxiliary fields, contact info on the back, navy-and-gold sample)…

Trade-off: The heaviest membership option to run: Apple passes need a paid Apple Developer account plus signing and push certificates, and event-day pass updates need a pass web service. Paper and the in-account card cover anyone who skips the wallet.

s_Account-A.text:
What: "Next up" dashboard for an adult member (Avery): a Needs-attention row (unpaid entry before the early-entry deadline, US Chess membership ending before an entered event, LCA membership ending in 21 days), then one date-ordered timeline that mixes entries, saved events (LCA and partner), deadlines and the home club's nights…

Borrowed from: NN/g + Baymard (current status and next action first; tracker), KingRegistration (US Chess expiry flagged against the event…

Trade-off: Showing saved events and club nights alongside entries makes a long page for active players, and the nightly US Chess check depends on lookups that can be slow or rate-limited.

s_Account-B.text:
What: Parent-first dashboard for Danielle: household header with everyone's chips, two needs-attention items (Leo has no US Chess ID before his first event; Maya's bye waiting on the director), one card per person (next events, section, payment, US Chess status, kid-sized milestone…

Borrowed from: AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc "Who's playing?" household picker, ChessRoster (one section panel per player…

Trade-off: The day view only shines on event days and needs pairings published through the site in real time; the rest of the year it is a preview, and the page is long for families with three kids.

s_Account-C.text:
What: One login, many roles (Chris: member, parent, club rep, tournament director, board rep) with no mode switch: role chips at the top name every role and jump to its section; a single "Today across your roles" list merges tasks with a worded role label (US Chess expiries among entrants, a bye request to approve, a board vote…

Borrowed from: NN/g on personalization and modes (accurate role-based sections, no switcher), GOV.UK task list (status in words)…

Trade-off: The page grows with every role, so a heavy volunteer gets a long scroll; the merged Today list needs careful ranking or one role's noise drowns the rest.

s_Work-A.text:
What: Tablet-first event-day console for the TD (The Baton Rouge Classic, Sun 9:14 AM before round 4): navy status band with a countdown, a round rail (check-in, rounds 1–5, prizes, rating report) and an offline/sync badge…

Borrowed from: Chesstide (per-round check-in badges with undo, 1/2/3 + arrow result entry, "Check-in All", event poster with QR…

Trade-off: Real-time sync plus offline editing is the hardest engineering on this board (two tablets editing the same round need conflict rules), texting players costs money per message, and player-reported results need a dispute flow TDs trust.

s_Clubs-A.text:
What: List and map side by side with lettered pins linked to the rows. Each row starts with when the club meets and a computed "Tonight" or next date, then name, venue and tags. Day and "Good for" chips filter list and pins together, and every row shows a Confirmed stamp or a Needs-check flag.

Borrowed from: Baymard (map beside the list), NC Chess Association (Last confirmed + Report outdated info), Seattle tags (quick filter chips)…

Trade-off: Every club needs a structured schedule and a confirmed date before the page works, and 25 rows make a long page at 1440px (about 2600px tall).

s_Clubs-B.text:
What: A statewide Monday–Sunday timetable of all 19 real meetings this week, with days as columns and morning/afternoon/evening as rows. A navy "Tonight" panel with a small map of tonight's clubs comes first.

Borrowed from: Saint Louis, Columbia and Downriver (statewide weekly grid; Downriver's real "no play on Saints game nights" skip rule)…

Trade-off: Clubs without a structured schedule (7 not listed, plus 3 monthly or seasonal) drop off the grid into side lists, and the 8-column table scrolls sideways on phones, where the Tonight panel does most of the work.

s_Clubs-C.text:
What: The 7 official regions as sections, each with a mini-map cropped to its clubs, its board seat (a rep with a Message button, or "Seat open · Volunteer", which also flags listings that need a check), its clubs with meeting lines, and its upcoming tournaments.

Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (region chips with counts, cards grouped by region, clubs keep their own entries)…

Trade-off: All 25 clubs must be assigned to a region first (blank in live data) and reps recruited. People near a border (Hammond, Picayune) may look in the wrong section, and cross-region questions like "who meets Tuesday?" are harder than in A or B.

s_Club-B.text:
What: A club-branded mini-site for Baton Rouge Chess Club. It has a colour band and tint, a logo slot, Follow and Add to calendar, and a "Next at the club" card built from both weekly nights. Anchor tabs lead to About (two ways to play, first-visit Q&A, a two-venue map, facts)…

Borrowed from: Strava clubs (club page with events, posts and a weekly leaderboard; join/follow), Downriver ("Your first visit" questions)…

Trade-off: It only pays off if the club rep keeps posting; with sparse content the tabs look empty (Club-C is the fallback). The leaderboard needs a results archive matched by US Chess ID, and some players won't want to be ranked, hence the opt-out.

s_Club-C.text:
What: A compact, honest profile for a club with little info (Gonzales Chess Club). A "2 of 7 details" meter puts "What we know" (missing facts stated plainly, each with an Add link) beside a "Help us complete this listing" form that takes a structured schedule (day, repeat rule, time, venue, cost, good-for, contact…

Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (freshness loop: Last confirmed, report/complete info, nearby clubs…

Trade-off: The page asks visitors for data, and unverified suggestions need a volunteer to review them. Without that, the queue goes stale and the page stays empty. It's also less inviting than a full club page, by design.

s_Start-Audit.text:
What: A factual audit of today's louisianachess.org: a 5-card "Fix first" strip (slideshow fails WCAG 2.2.2, 1.54:1 focus ring, 2.28:1 gold text, colour-only status dots, Register card below the player list on phones), then a table of 17 areas with KEEP strengths and FIX problems rated High/Med/Low…

Borrowed from: codebase-inventory.md (page layouts, data model, the 52 UX issues), ux-evidence.md "Current site" findings and file map (WCAG…

Trade-off: severity is a reasoned rating from the research, not usage data; it is a snapshot of the code as read (the ticket-reply bug is marked "worth verifying"), and the board runs 1,600px taller than planned to fit 17 areas without clipping.

s_Sources.text:
What: One index of every source behind the board, 236 lines in four balanced columns: peer federations (27), tournament platforms (14), clubs and chess brands incl. Louisiana (34), cross-domain sites (53), evidence (62 lines covering NN/g, Baymard, GOV.UK, USWDS, WCAG 2.2, practitioners, platform docs and studies…

Borrowed from: the reference and "Sites examined" sections of all seven research files.

Trade-off: dense by design (a lookup page, not a read-through); links are plain text; related evidence articles share a line so ~120 references fit in 62 lines; the board is 1,350px taller than planned to avoid clipping.

s_Scan-C.text:
What: A printable notation kit that feeds the Scanner, as three Letter sheets: a scan-ready LCA scoresheet (four corner marks, one comb-ticked box per move, 50 moves on the front, fill-in result boxes, and when printed from the pairings a typed header plus a sheet-ID QR), a kids' notation cheat sheet (square names, piece letters…

Borrowed from: Saint Louis Chess Club's free notation workbook and the clubs-brands "notation kit, Scanner, analysis" loop…

Trade-off: pre-printed sheets add a print step that needs final pairings, and reading marks, QR and result boxes is new backend work; players will still bring their own sheets, so the scanner must keep working without marks…

s_Event-B.text:
What: Flagship hub for the 2027 Louisiana State Championship. It has a navy banner with a countdown and "23 of 160 registered", sticky tabs (Overview · Sections & prizes · Entries · Pairings · Standings · Hotel & travel · Past champions) and a live-strip slot that appears only Sep 4–6.

Borrowed from: Grand Chess Tour / FIDE Candidates (event tabs as a mini-microsite), Tata Steel Chess (countdown)…

Trade-off: A lot of page for one weekend a year. Pairings and Standings sit empty for 11 months, and volunteers must feed in the hotel, meeting room and agenda details or the hub looks half-built.

s_Event-C.text:
What: The same 2027 Paul Morphy Open page at three moments, side by side. Before (Tue, Jun 1): price today, how full each section is, who's coming, and Register in the phone bar. During (Sat, Jun 12, 7:40 PM, live Round 3): a "Your board" card, pairings by section, TD notes, round alerts and a site-wide live banner.

Borrowed from: Marshall / Columbia / Norway Chess (live mode via the site banner), start.gg and Chesstide (round and check-in banners)…

Trade-off: The automatic switch is only as good as the data. A late result entry or a section that finishes hours after the others leaves the page in the wrong mode, so TDs need an override and the edge cases need testing.

s_Event-E.text:
What: Internal LCA page for a real clearinghouse listing: Mississippi State Championship, Sat–Sun, Oct 17–18, Canton, MS, Mississippi Chess Association. It has one gold "Register on organizer site" exit and a facts card with the same fields in the same order on every partner event, which says plainly what the feed lacks (fees…

Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (internal pages for clearinghouse events, consistent facts card, "Register on organizer site ↗"…

Trade-off: Partner pages are thin by nature (no fees or status in the feed), and the drive times and change alerts depend on geocoding and a reliable daily diff. Every Register click still sends the visitor away.

s_Reg-C.text:
What: A one-page household checkout for the Paul Morphy Open & Morphy Scholastic. Danielle Robichaux ticks saved players (herself, Maya, Leo; no child logins). Each player gets a panel showing only the sections they can enter by rating, one yes/no grade box for grade-capped sections ("Maya is in 8th grade or below")…

Borrowed from: ChessRoster (one section panel per player, one fee table, one payment), AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc ("Who's…

Trade-off: A long page for a single adult entering one section, and the edge cases multiply: playing up, one child's section filling mid-checkout, partial refunds on one payment. Passing on the processing fee is a board policy call.

s_Reg-D.text:
What: Guest-first quick entry for the Paul Morphy Open, on desktop and two phones. Typing a US Chess ID fills in name, rating and membership expiry ("Found: Sam Nguyen · 1650 · member through Nov 30, 2027"), with search by name as a fallback.

Borrowed from: KingRegistration and ECF (US Chess ID or last-name lookup fills name, rating, expiry), Luma (guest-first, account after payment)…

Trade-off: Guest entries scatter player data outside accounts (duplicates, a typo'd email locks someone out of their manage link). It also depends on a reliable US Chess lookup, and players without an ID still need a slower path.

s_About-A.text:
What: Transparency hub for About: who LCA is (real stats), a next-board-meeting card (Tue, Nov 10 · agenda · add to calendar), bylaws as a web page with per-article "Changed" flags, a records list where every item carries a status and last-updated date, a plain-language minutes recap tagged Notable/Routine, "write to a seat…

Borrowed from: Chicago Councilmatic (next-meeting card + plain-language recap), NN/g and data.gov (minutes and bylaws as web pages with "Last…

Trade-off: Only builds trust if the Secretary and Treasurer keep it current; stale stamps or empty [Amount] cells would advertise neglect, and every meeting needs a plain-language recap.

s_Club-A.text:
What: Visit-first Downriver Chess Club page: "Tonight, 7:00 PM · Mon, Oct 5" as the headline, Turtle Bay (1119 Decatur St) with a mini map and honest access notes (two flights of stairs, a bar, parking placeholder), cost and G/15 in plain words, a four-step "Your first visit" story with a before-you-go card…

Borrowed from: Downriver Chess (its "Your first visit!" story, honest Turtle Bay notes, no club night on Saints games)…

Trade-off: Downriver is the richest case; most of the 25 clubs can't supply venue notes, first-visit copy or photos, so their pages would be mostly brackets unless paired with a compact fallback (Club-C).

s_Clubs-D.text:
What: Directory of all 25 real clubs as A–Z cards (logo slot or initials, club-colour dot, meeting day/time and venue, time control in plain words, up to three tags, "Confirmed" month) with search, a region mini-map and region list with counts, quick chips with live counts (Meets today 6, Weekends, Kids welcome, Rated, Free…

Borrowed from: North Carolina Chess Association (region chips with counts, club cards, "Last confirmed" + "Report outdated info")…

Trade-off: 25 cards make a long scroll and shrink geography to a mini-map; most cards will show initials rather than logos; an A–Z bar is heavy for 25 clubs.

s_Event-A.text:
What: 2027 Paul Morphy Open (Sample details) with fact tiles that translate chess shorthand, a sticky registration card (38 of 60, section picker, early/regular/late ladder with dates, member price, Register / Register my family, plus the button's other states: opens-remind, waitlist, registered, live, final)…

Borrowed from: Luma (sticky two-column card, button states, "38 registered — names and 36 others"), Chess67 / ChessRoster (registration card…

Trade-off: Very long page that needs a lot of TD-entered data per event (caps, price dates, venue notes); a public rating-sorted entry list puts kids' names and ratings on the page (normal at rated events, but parents notice).

s_Event-D.text:
What: Festival microsite for the Paul Morphy Open + Morphy Scholastic + Friday Night Blitz (Sample, Fri–Sun, Jun 11–13, 2027): sticky festival bar, photo hero with countdown and "112 players registered across 3 events", all three events with sections, eligibility as one yes/no box, fees and "X of Y", an Open + Blitz bundle…

Borrowed from: London Chess Classic and the Ken Ferguson Memorial (festival grouping with side events)…

Trade-off: Pays off for one or two flagship weekends a year and needs a volunteer for hotel, sponsor, speaker and venue content; a second event template to maintain.

s_Home-A.text:
What: The next registerable event (Lafayette Open 2026) as the hero card — weekday dates, check-in and round 1, time control in plain words, sections, 38 of 60 with spots left and the next price deadline, Register from $30 — with an inset of the same slot in "Live · Round 3 pairings posted" mode…

Borrowed from: Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association ("Next Event" block) and Tata Steel (countdown)…

Trade-off: The hero only shines when the next event registers on LCA; when it's a partner listing it loses the count and Register, and the page is long and dense below the fold.

s_Home-B.text:
What: Search-first homepage: one box for tournaments, clubs and players with grouped type-ahead (shown mid-search for "baton"), quick picks (This weekend · Scholastic · Near me · Rated · Free), stats that are links (25+ clubs, 7 regions, 11 tournaments, 300+ members), a next-up line, then compact panels: next 5 tournaments…

Borrowed from: North Carolina Chess Association (search-first hero with clickable stats), Chess67 / ChessRoster time chips and Seattle Chess…

Trade-off: Search is only as good as its index and the US Chess lookup; a search box shows less life than an event hero, and many small panels compete for attention.

s_Home-D.text:
What: Newspaper front page: dateline + "Updated" time, a bulletin line (Lafayette Open as a partner event; turns live on LCA event days), a lead State Championship recap (Sample) with section winners, a results box with the tiebreak explained and an upset of the weekend, a coming-up rail incl.

Borrowed from: Substack (Newspaper/Feature hero modes), Central Florida (recap with winners box), World Chess Hall of Fame (champion cards)…

Trade-off: Needs steady editorial output (recaps, photos, short posts); without a volunteer writer the dateline makes staleness obvious within weeks.

s_Home-E.text:
What: Three photo doors ("I want to play" / "My child plays" / "I run a club or tournament"), three links each landing on shared, pre-filtered pages (landing named in grey), an escape row for people who fit none or several, next events grouped open / scholastic / LCA championships (Sample 2027 LCA dates, "18 of 80")…

Borrowed from: Charlotte Chess Center (three-door branching, without its lead form), Ireland's federation (audience row) tempered by NN/g's…

Trade-off: Doors make visitors pick an identity and add a click; a playing parent fits two doors, and the grouped lists repeat events.

s_Live-D.text:
What: Hall TV screen for the 2027 Paul Morphy Open (Sample): Round 3 U1800 pairings in two big columns (colour, name, rating, points going in), round start with countdown and posted time, byes spelled out, a QR to the phone view ("Your board, on your phone"), a round timeline…

Borrowed from: ChessRoster (/live TV mode cycling pairings and standings), Chesstide / Chess-Results / Chess67's Campbell story (hall QR to the…

Trade-off: Only for LCA-run events paired on the site, and needs a screen plus laptop at the venue; 15-second paging means a player may wait up to a minute for their section.

s_Looks-3-Minimal-Tile.text:
What: Style tile for "Modern Tech-Minimal — the club, engineered": idea / best for / watch out, Geist + Geist Mono + one Instrument Serif accent, light and dark palettes with contrast ratios (gold as fill only on white, #866a1e for gold text), components (navy glass header with ⌘K search, buttons, all status tags, US Chess ID input…

Borrowed from: visual-directions §3 references — Vercel Geist (font, 6/12px radii), Linear (near-black surfaces, quiet tables)…

Trade-off: Closest to today's site and cheapest to adopt, but reads as generic SaaS unless notation, clocks and coordinates carry the chess character.

s_Nav-IA.text:
What: The ~40 pages filed three ways side by side — (1) Task and topic (recommended; About as a click dropdown), (2) Audience hubs with "in 2/3 hubs" duplication badges, (3) Lean four + More — each with pros/cons, a "Today" column describing the live Navbar/Footer and its four issues, and a table of where Scanner, Champions…

Borrowed from: NN/g and GOV.UK (audience menus fail; "For parents" as a hub page, USA Swimming as the counter-example)…

Trade-off: A planning board, not a design; the recommended bar is full at 1024px and moves Scanner to the footer, which needs usage data and a parent tree test to confirm.

s_News-A.text:
What: News as one featured results story (State Championship, Sample) with section winners, pinned items that expire on a set date, month-grouped dated rows with category chips and counts, a "From our Facebook page" rail fed server-side, a "Post club news" prompt for reps, "Load 10 more" and a yearly archive.

Borrowed from: Substack (Feature hero mode), Chess Scotland (pinned news), NN/g (rows not cards, "Load more" instead of infinite scroll)…

Trade-off: The featured slot needs a steady supply of recaps with photos; pins and categories add an editorial job.

s_News-B.text:
What: One chronological stream grouped by day (Today / Yesterday / dates) mixing LCA posts, results (top three), club news with a club-colour dot, Facebook posts and announcements, each with a type label and time; short items read in full, type chips with counts plus a club filter, a pinned announcement, older posts a month at a time.

Borrowed from: The Verge Storystream (short posts between full articles), Ghost's Source theme (single feed with byline and date)…

Trade-off: With 16 of 60 items from Facebook the stream can feel noisy and bury the big recaps; it depends on a merged feed with consistent type labels.

s_Reg-A.text:
What: Registration stays inside the event page's sticky card: five states beside a dimmed 2027 Paul Morphy Open page — at rest with prices and 38 of 60; "Who's playing?" (Danielle, Maya, Leo, someone else); section + one-box eligibility + byes by round with day and time, ineligible sections greyed with the reason…

Borrowed from: Chess67 / ChessRoster / Luma (registration card in the right column), AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc ("Who's playing?"…

Trade-off: A narrow card gets cramped for families with per-player sections and byes, and on phones it becomes a full-height sheet anyway.

s_Reg-B.text:
What: Five phones, one question per screen for Jordan Lee (Sample): who's playing, then which section (only eligible ones, priced with early + member discounts, "Which section fits me?"), then byes by round plus an inline US Chess ID check whose expiry warning never blocks…

Borrowed from: GOV.UK (one question per page, check your answers), ChessRoster (step-by-step Player → Section → Byes → Pay)…

Trade-off: More taps than a one-card form for regulars who already know their section, and a separate flow from the event page.

s_Schol-A.text:
What: Parent guide to a first scholastic tournament: quick facts, a numbered jump bar, a check-in-to-awards timeline (Sample times, "~" for rounds that start when the last ends), a what-to-bring checklist, chess words in plain English, grade-band sections, costs (real $5 / $25 memberships, Sample entries…

Borrowed from: New South Wales / Virginia / Ireland / England federations ("Your first tournament" path)…

Trade-off: Very long and content-heavy; times and fees must stay in sync with real events, and the lunch discount implies asking families something the privacy card doesn't list.

s_Tourn-A.text:
What: Month-grouped agenda (16 events Oct–Dec, LCA and Gulf South partner) with date blocks, status in words, "X of Y registered" with fill bars and deadlines on LCA rows, lighter partner rows that say where entry happens, one row of filter chips (When · Type · Region · Rated · LCA-run / Partner) with removable applied chips…

Borrowed from: the federations research's top idea (one chip row incl. LCA-run vs clearinghouse)…

Trade-off: Partner rows (12 of 16) are thin by necessity and dominate the list; Calendar and Map are only tabs here.

s_Live-A.text:
What: Three phones across one Saturday evening (all Sample data, matching Live-D's Round 3). (1) The round-ready banner, then find-your-board by typing a few letters, with a follow star on each match. (2) A pinned "Board 7 · You have White · vs Sam Nguyen 1650 · starts 7:00 PM" card in big type, with a text-size toggle…

Borrowed from: Chess67 (round-posted message "You are playing White against … on board 4"), start.gg / melee.gg (pinned "your board" card)…

Trade-off: Results reported by players need the opponent's confirmation plus a TD review queue, or disputes move from the TD table to the website. Alerts only help if the TD publishes pairings on the site the moment they're made.

s_Live-B.text:
What: The main live pairings page, shown at 8:41 PM Saturday with Round 3 in progress and 5 of 13 U1800 results in. It has round tabs and section chips with counts, type-to-find (it highlights the matching row), by-board or A–Z order, a text-size toggle remembered on the device, and "Updated 1 min ago" with refresh every 60 s.

Borrowed from: IRLchess / SwissSys (board rows with scores, "Bd · White (2½) · result · Black"), SwissSys (by-board and alphabetical orders)…

Trade-off: One page for every section means long scrolling at big events. Collapsing the other sections keeps it short but hides boards that spectators may expect to see.

s_Live-C.text:
What: Final U1800 results (Sample data, internally consistent with Live-D's Round 3). One place-ordered "standings + crosstable" table in SwissSys style. Round cells read like "W ○ 17": letter, tint and a hollow (White) or filled (Black) dot, so colour is never the only signal. Scores use ½.

Borrowed from: ChessRoster / SwissSys (standings with W17 / L2 / D3 / H / B / U cells and a prize column…

Trade-off: The combined table is wide (14 columns) and dense. On phones it leans on the column chooser and the player card, and opponent pairing numbers need tap-to-jump to feel friendly.

s_Live-E.text:
What: Six letter-size sheets (560×725) on a neutral ground, each captioned, all built from the same live data (Sample, consistent with Live-B/C/D). (1) Hall poster with a QR placeholder drawn as an SVG grid, the short link louisianachess.org/morphy27, the round times and "Phones off and away once clocks start".

Borrowed from: Chess67 Campbell story (two posted QR codes ended "the frantic scramble to print")…

Trade-off: Paper never fully goes away at a volunteer event, and two sources of truth (sheet and site) can drift unless results circled on paper are entered right away. The per-board QR cards add a setup step for whoever lays out the tables.

s_Looks-1-Heritage-Tile.text:
What: Style tile for "Heritage Club — since 1915": Libre Caslon Display headlines, Source Serif 4 text with true small caps and tabular figures, IBM Plex Mono for notation; cream paper, navy ink, gold only for rules/seals/text on navy; a round seal built from the rook-shaped mark…

Borrowed from: Pentagram's World Chess identity ("a study, not a stage": wood, brass, paper), Marshall Chess Club (heritage from copy and type…

Trade-off: Weakest at fast-changing live data, and serif small caps get fussy in dense admin/workspace UI; brand gold can never be text on cream (2.05:1), so it recedes to rules and seals.

s_Looks-1-Heritage-Page.text:
What: The shared sample page set as a printed club program: cream header with Caslon wordmark, small-caps nav and a thick–thin rule; "Lafayette Open 2026" hero with a When/Where/Format/Hosted-by ledger and a navy–cream duotone photo in a cream mat; a ruled "since 1915 · 300+ · 25+ · 7" band…

Borrowed from: The Masters (leaderboard-first, honor-board standings), Marshall Chess Club (history told in copy, plain interface)…

Trade-off: Calm and trustworthy but slow-feeling: no live state, and the duotone dulls photos that sell scholastic events; the serif-heavy header needs care at phone widths.

s_Looks-2-Editorial-Tile.text:
What: Style tile for "Editorial Sports — results as news": Newsreader 800 headlines (proportional figures), Schibsted Grotesk for text/UI with 900-caps dark-gold kickers, Chivo Mono for agate data; white and newsprint grounds, 3px-navy-over-1px-ink rules instead of cards; status tags plus an "Upset" label…

Borrowed from: Grand Chess Tour (fixed 16:9 event tiles linking Overview/Players/Results), Freestyle Chess (credited venue photos)…

Trade-off: Needs a volunteer to write a headline and pick a photo after every event, or it goes stale fast; three families and big type are heavier than a utility look, and the newspaper density can feel busy on phones.

s_Looks-2-Editorial-Page.text:
What: The shared sample page as a newspaper front page: dated top strip with Donate / Log in / gold Join LCA, a centered Newsreader nameplate over the 3px-navy/1px-ink rule and a caps section nav, then a pausable results ticker (Sample data)…

Borrowed from: The Athletic (front-page lead + modules; named in the brief, not fetched), The Ringer (recurring "Upset"/"Rating movers"…

Trade-off: Only as good as the last headline: with no one writing after events, the lead falls back to "next event" and the report slot goes stale; the ticker is extra motion that must stay pausable; heaviest font load of the two looks.

s_Looks-3-Minimal-Page.text:
What: The sample homepage in Modern Tech-Minimal, matched to the published tile: a sticky 92%-navy glass header with ⌘K search; a next-event hero on the 8-column a–h / 8–1 dot grid with a navy-to-gold duotone photo; events as a quiet table with "in N days"; a Mon–Sat club agenda; standings with W/D/L chips and a fixed Player column…

Borrowed from: Vercel's Geist design system (Geist + Geist Mono, 6/12px radii), Linear (lists as quiet tables, almost no motion)…

Trade-off: The calmest and cheapest of the seven, and the most generic. Only coordinates, notation and real data make it read as chess or Louisiana, and the duotone mutes the warmth of the photos.

s_Looks-Compare.text:
What: All seven looks side by side in a 4+3 grid. Each card is set in the look's own fonts (all 21 families come from one css2 request) and shows a 5-swatch strip with hex values, a header slice with its primary "Join LCA" button, and "Registration open" / "Live · Round 3" tags in its style, plus a "Best for" line.

Borrowed from: visual-directions.md's seven directions and their references: Pentagram's World Chess identity and Marshall Chess Club…

Trade-off: Each card is a thumbnail, so subtleties such as contrast pairs, motifs and photo treatment only show on the full tiles and pages. Twenty-one families in one request is heavy, but only this board needs it.

s_Start-Principles.text:
What: A one-page doc on #fbfaf6. On the left are ten LCA design principles, each with a one-line rule, a concrete example and the checklist rows it maps to, followed by an 8-line "What the evidence settles" summary.

Borrowed from: the sources behind ux-evidence.md (NN/g, Baymard, GOV.UK, USWDS, W3C WAI / WCAG 2.2)…

Trade-off: One-line rows compress some nuance, such as the mega-menu rule and the Core Web Vitals targets, so the source checklist stays the reference in a dispute. It is a static checklist, not a scoring tool.

s_Looks-4-Swiss-Tile.text:
What: The style tile is itself a chessboard — files a–h run across the top and bottom, ranks 8→1 down both rails, and every block is addressed by its square ("c5 · Status"). It covers Archivo wide 800/900 + Fragment Mono, a flush 8-swatch palette strip with ratios, 0-radius flat components, a 4×2-square event card…

Borrowed from: Metric's Norwegian Chess Federation identity (grid + diagonal "bishop lines"), International Typographic Style…

Trade-off: The most systematic and the coldest of the seven: wide display type forces short headlines, gold can only ever be a field, and the green/yellow/purple logo has no place in it. Test it with older members before committing.

s_Looks-4-Swiss-Page.text:
What: The homepage sample in Swiss Grid. A navy header sits over an a–h file strip, and ranks 8→1 run down the left rail as section addresses (a8 Next event, a6 Tournaments, a5 Clubs…). The type-led hero sets "Lafayette / Open 2026" in wide black at 104px over a When/Where/Type/Ages fact grid…

Borrowed from: Metric's Norwegian Chess Federation identity (grid, addressed sections), Swissted (type-led poster hero)…

Trade-off: It's long and rigid. The wide type and square photo add about 300px, the week strip scrolls sideways on phones, and it may feel cold to parents and older casual players.

s_Looks-5-Louisiana-Tile.text:
What: The style tile for "Louisiana Rooted — statewide, with an accent". Fraunces display (opsz 144, soft 100) sits over Bricolage Grotesque text and DM Mono data on magnolia paper, under a cypress top band.

Borrowed from: The Historic New Orleans Collection (mustard and dark green on cream, disciplined grid)…

Trade-off: It's the warmest and most place-specific option, but kitsch is one step away. It also leans on data the site doesn't have yet (a parish for each club, event and champion).

s_Looks-5-Louisiana-Page.text:
What: The homepage sample in Louisiana Rooted. A cypress-ruled magnolia header carries the rook mark in cypress and a Fraunces wordmark. The editorial hero sets "Lafayette Open 2026" in Fraunces with "Lafayette Parish", a South Central chip and a Partner event tag ("registration is on the organizer's site")…

Borrowed from: The Historic New Orleans Collection (cream, green and mustard in a disciplined grid), 64 Parishes (identity from specifics…

Trade-off: It's the longest page in the set because of its newsletter spacing. The parish and region chips need data that's blank today (regions are empty, there's no parish field), so the Greater New Orleans club shows "[Parish]".

s_Looks-6-Scholastic-Tile.text:
What: Style tile for Bright Scholastic: Baloo 2 / Nunito / Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono on cream with navy as the anchor, one color per section (K–3 coral, K–5 mint, K–8 sky, K–12 grape), press-down buttons with a hard navy shadow, checker-strip section tabs, a pawn-to-queen sign-up track, podium medal circles…

Borrowed from: ONY's World Schools Team Chess Championship identity (pawn mascot, playful marks on strict type), Story Time Chess (rounded…

Trade-off: Five hues can tip into "toy store". It only stays credible to coaches if navy carries all text and buttons and color only ever means section, so it works as a section theme, not site-wide.

s_Looks-6-Scholastic-Page.text:
What: The shared sample page in Bright Scholastic. A cream header with an app-icon mark and a four-color checker strip; a press-down hero card for the Lafayette Open with a "5 days to go" sticker and a ticket-style date…

Borrowed from: Story Time Chess and ChessKid (friendly, parent-first tone), ONY's WSTC identity (checker strip, pawn motif)…

Trade-off: Chunky 48px+ targets and card rows make the same content about 20% taller than the 2400px plan (about 2,900px), and the playful tone fits Scholastic far better than the home page shown here.

s_Looks-7-Broadcast-Tile.text:
What: Style tile for Broadcast Night: Barlow Condensed / Barlow / JetBrains Mono (ligatures off), with Big Shoulders Display for round banners only, on navy-black. Gold is the live accent; live red carries dark text only; elevation comes from lighter surfaces.

Borrowed from: Lichess broadcasts (LIVE and round before the title) and the lila source (shrinking 4px clock bar…

Trade-off: Dark, condensed and data-dense is right for a dim hall or a projector but tiring for long reading. Live red is a trap (white on #ff4757 is only 3.34), so this has to stay an event-day theme, not the site default.

s_Looks-7-Broadcast-Page.text:
What: The shared sample page in Broadcast Night, previewed in event-day mode (labelled "Event-day preview: Sat, Oct 10, 8:15 PM" with a Night mode toggle). It has a header status line ("LIVE · R3 · Lafayette Open 2026 · Round 3 in progress · pairings posted 6:42 PM")…

Borrowed from: Lichess broadcasts (LIVE and round before the title), Saint Louis Chess Club ("Open today" header status line)…

Trade-off: The live hero only fits event days, and this board doesn't show the non-live fallback (a countdown). Also, the Lafayette Open is a partner event, so real live data would exist only for LCA-run events or partners using LCA's pairing engine.

s_Nav-Header.text:
What: Five full-width desktop headers on real pages, each with one state open — H1 Refined (six visible sections, click-open About menu showing "You are here", fixed Donate · Log in · Join LCA), H2 Two-tier (thin live bar: "Lafayette Open · Round 3 pairings posted · Find your board", plus a chip row of the line's other states)…

Borrowed from: NN/g (visible nav beats hamburger, click-not-hover submenus with carets, show current location, utility nav top-right…

Trade-off: H2 and H5 only pay off if pairings are actually published on the site during events; H4 adds a search index to maintain for a ~40-page site where list filters may be enough…

s_Nav-Mobile.text:
What: Four 390 px phone navs — M1 Combo bar (LCA mark + always-visible "Tournaments" + bordered "Menu" button; open sheet with the current section expanded as "You are here", Scoresheet scanner under Tournaments, then Donate · Log in · Join LCA and Facebook/Contact/Help)…

Borrowed from: NN/g (combo nav used 86% vs 57% for hidden menus; labelled, bordered Menu button…

Trade-off: M2's tab bar spends 72 px on every screen and its "Events" label differs from the desktop "Tournaments"; M3 hides everything behind one tap; M4 depends on pairings being published on the site and on players being logged in.

s_Nav-Footer.text:
What: Three complete footers — F1 Refined navy four columns (Play incl. Scoresheet scanner / Community incl. Facebook / About LCA / Contact with LouisianaChess@gmail.com) beside a brand block with Join LCA + Donate, and an affiliate base line…

Borrowed from: federations research (NC and England four-column footers with governance links and an affiliate line)…

Trade-off: F2's doors repeat calls to action already in the header and homepage; F3's freshness line backfires if the numbers look stale (it needs clubs to actually confirm), and the digest adds an email list LCA must manage (consent, unsubscribes).

s_Home-C.text:
What: The homepage is a living weekly agenda: a navy hero with the identity line and a computed summary ("Mon, Oct 5 – Sun, Oct 11 · 19 club meetings at 15 clubs · Lafayette Open Sat–Sun · National Chess Day"), last/this/next week switcher, region chips and "Near me"…

Borrowed from: clubs-brands top ideas #1–2 ("Tonight / This week" strip and a statewide weekly grid), NN/g homepage guidance (say who you are…

Trade-off: The page is only as good as club schedules, so a stale or missing schedule shows in public on the front page; newcomers get less storytelling (no photo hero, no news lead), and the grid is dense on phones…

s_Home-F.text:
What: Map-first homepage: an identity line + "Chess near you, anywhere in Louisiana" with a City/ZIP field and "Use my location"; a statewide map beside a synced "Near you" list (all 25 real clubs as pins, clusters for New Orleans Metro "8" and Baton Rouge "2", rings on the 6 clubs meeting tonight…

Borrowed from: Baymard (95% used a map placed beside the list vs 65% who never found it on list-only sites), NC federation (clickable stats)…

Trade-off: The map hero pushes event details below the first screen, so it serves "what's near me" better than "register for this weekend"; region data is blank in the live site today…

s_Home-Phones.text:
What: Home options A, B, C and E at 390 px under one combo-nav app header (visible "Tournaments" link plus a labelled Menu): A = Lafayette Open hero with an inset of its event-day live state; B = type-ahead search with results grouped by type plus stat links; C = Mon–Sun strip of the 19 real meetings with tonight first and "On now"…

Borrowed from: NN/g (combo nav beats hidden menus), ChessRoster and Marshall/Columbia/Norway (new-round banner, live mode)…

Trade-off: A spends the first screen on one event (strong when an LCA event is near, thin between events); B only feels instant with a real index behind it; C is only as good as the clubs' structured times; E costs one extra tap before content.

s_Tourn-Phones.text:
What: The tournaments list on a phone in four states: a month-grouped agenda with a Louisiana chip applied (removable, "11 events", Subscribe); a near-full-height filter sheet (When / Where with state counts and a region row / Type / Where you register / rated-only) whose button shows the live total "Show 16 events"…

Borrowed from: Baymard and AllTrails (filter panel with an Apply button and live count, removable applied chips)…

Trade-off: The sheet covers the list while you choose (the live count compensates). The Monday-first grid breaks the US Sunday-first habit to keep weekend events on one line.

s_Event-Phones.text:
What: The event page on a phone with a sticky bottom Register bar in three states ("$40 early · Register · $40", then "Registered · Change section or byes"), the top of the 2027 Paul Morphy Open above the fold (weekday dates, plain-language G/90+30, 38 of 60, early/regular/late ladder)…

Borrowed from: Luma, Meetup and Dice (one action button whose state changes: Register / Registered / Join waitlist / Closed)…

Trade-off: A fixed bar permanently takes about 90 px of a small screen and has to be kept out of the way of the in-page tabs. Listing young players by first name and last initial departs from full-name entry lists some players expect.

s_Clubs-Phones.text:
What: The clubs directory on a phone in four states: a list sorted by next meeting where each row leads with when ("On now · until 5:00 PM", "Tonight 5:30 PM"), with "Confirmed Sep 2026 · Report outdated info" and a floating Map button…

Borrowed from: Airbnb (linked pins), Yelp ("Search this area" and the list/map toggle), Baymard (map findability on list-first sites…

Trade-off: Sorting by next meeting needs every club's schedule as structured data (7 clubs have none and drop to the end). Day columns show only about two days at a time, so a statewide glance needs swipes.

s_Schol-Phones.text:
What: Scholastic for parents on phones at the venue: a live day view of the (real) New Orleans Youth Chess November Meet showing each family child's board and colour, the round in progress on a timeline (check-in to awards, later times marked as estimates), "Updated 1 min ago" and an opt-in round-ready alert…

Borrowed from: AskFRED (first-tournament guide with a glossary and a day-of checklist), ChessRoster ("Round 3 pairings are ready" banner) and…

Trade-off: The live view only works for LCA-run events where pairings come out of LCA's own engine, not for partner meets. Alerts need push permission (iOS only for home-screen web apps), so email is the fallback.

s_Schol-B.text:
What: A five-rung staircase (club night → first scholastic meet → NOLA Youth Chess Grand Prix → LCA State Scholastic → Nationals) whose rungs list real upcoming events, then live Grand Prix standings by grade band with team standings and follow-a-player alerts, auto-awarded milestones…

Borrowed from: pathway ladder with "qualified via" (FIDE Candidates); series leaderboard (Downriver youth page, Grand Chess Tour standings)…

Trade-off: The Grand Prix meets are partner-run, so automatic points only work if organizers run meets in LCA's TD tools or upload final standings; public kids' standings and the scoring rules need organizer and parent sign-off.

s_Schol-C.text:
What: A scholastic hub with an audience switch and three doors (Parents, Coaches, Schools), one merged table of real scholastic events (LCA vs partner sign-up, iCal subscription), a map-based youth program finder over the 5 youth programs plus 3 kid-friendly clubs…

Borrowed from: audience row (Ireland); parent page order (England Football); "For parents" as a hub (NN/g)…

Trade-off: It is a long page that tries to serve three audiences at once, and team entry adds a new coach role, parent-confirmation emails and invoice handling for volunteers to support.

s_News-C.text:
What: News as five labelled sections (Results, Announcements, From the clubs, Scholastic, Board updates), each a short dated list of 3–4 rows with its own "See all", "In my digest" toggle and RSS, under a pinned announcement…

Borrowed from: one block per tag with "Show more" (Ghost Headline); short grouped teasers ending in "See all" (Harvard design system)…

Trade-off: Five sections need steady posting; a thin section (Board updates) looks stale fast, and auto-posted results read flat until someone writes the recap.

s_News-D.text:
What: A recap article template for every LCA event: a TD-only draft bar (filled in from final standings), headline, byline and fact chips, hero photo and lede, a winner card per section, an Open standings snippet with round-by-round results…

Borrowed from: bylined recap with section winners, ratings, top-board games and rating-report link (Central Florida Chess Club)…

Trade-off: Auto-drafts make recaps cheap but tempt publishing tables with bracketed gaps; someone still has to write the story and pick the game, and photos of kids need a consent and take-down routine.

s_About-B.text:
What: A board page built around "who do I call": a "Who represents me?" lookup (club, city or ZIP) that routes a message to the right rep and falls back to the whole board when the seat is open; officer cards with role, term, one-line duties and Message…

Borrowed from: board as two groups with open seats labeled (Michigan, Texas); regional directors list (Texas)…

Trade-off: Empty seats and "none listed yet" for quiet regions become very visible, and the lookup only works once clubs have confirmed regions (blank in live data today).

s_Tourn-B.text:
What: Master–detail list. A compact, month-grouped list (16 events) drives a sticky preview pane with the facts, sections and fees, live per-section counts, household checkout and Register (or "Register on organizer site"). The selected event is kept in the URL.

Borrowed from: NN/g (side panel instead of a pop-up; lists over cards for comparing), Luma (status slot plus "N going"…

Trade-off: the two panes need about 1200px. On tablets and phones the layout falls back to list, then a full-screen sheet, so "preview without losing your place" only works on desktop. The pane also gets long for LCA events.

s_Tourn-C.text:
What: The rebuilt calendar works as a navigator. A 9-month season strip (counts split into LCA and partner) and a clean Monday-first month grid sit beside a week-grouped agenda. In the grid, Sat–Sun events draw as one bar, today is marked, deadline and "entries open" ticks show, and a gold frame marks the week in view.

Borrowed from: Hund, Dowell & Mueller 2014 (a list beats a grid across month breaks, so the grid only navigates)…

Trade-off: the two views must stay in sync (scroll-spy moves the grid frame, and tapping a day scrolls the list). Big weekends get busy (Oct 24 stacks three bars). On phones the grid stacks above the list and the side-by-side navigation is lost.

s_Tourn-D.text:
What: Split map view. On the left, a list sorted by estimated drive time from a typed city or ZIP (or "Use my location"). On the right, a Gulf South map: filled pins for LCA events, hollow pins for partner events, clusters, and 100/200/300-mile rings.

Borrowed from: Baymard (split view, map beside the list, never in a pop-up), US Chess tournament search (distance from a ZIP code)…

Trade-off: drive times need geocoding plus a routing API and caching, and they are still estimates. Houston and the Jackson area cluster at state zoom. On phones the map stacks above the list and eats the screen.

s_Tourn-E.text:
What: A dense, sortable power table of all 25 upcoming events. Date and Event are frozen; the other columns are City · Type · Rating · Sections · Entries/cap (with mini bars) · Status (with the next deadline) · Source. Saved views sit in a tab bar, each with email alerts, its own .ics feed and a shareable URL.

Borrowed from: NAChessHub (dense list columns: date · state · city · type · rating · time control · organizer)…

Trade-off: it's intimidating for newcomers and parents, so it belongs behind the view switch, not as the default. It also exposes how thin the partner listings are ("Not listed", "Not in feed"), because the feed carries no sections, fees or status.

s_Work-B.text:
What: Club rep workspace (Houma Chess Club) built around the freshness loop: "Is this still accurate?" with one-tap confirm and visitor reports, a Tonight switch (on / moved / cancelled → club page + follower email), a structured-schedule club page editor with live card preview, club news with "Suggest for LCA News"…

Borrowed from: NC ("Last confirmed" stamp + "Report outdated info"), England Football (clubs manage their own listing)…

Trade-off: A lot for a volunteer who logs in twice a year (the emailed one-tap check and the Tonight switch have to carry it), and showing members' renewal status to reps needs an explicit privacy rule; board is 200px taller than planned.

s_Work-C.text:
What: Admin home at /admin with K's grouped sidebar (queues first) and one merged "Needs attention" queue — approvals, support tickets, board inbox, failed emails and club-listing gaps — where every row has an owner, waiting time and its own action button…

Borrowed from: Luma and Strava (approval queues; Luma's "pending approval by the calendar admin")…

Trade-off: The merged queue needs one item model across five existing systems and someone who actually owns assignment; with two or three admins the owner column may go unused. Board is 150px taller than planned.

s_Work-D.text:
What: One-page setup checklist for an LCA event (Paul Morphy Open 2027, cloned from 2026) with quick-add section presets (Open/U1800/U1400/U1000 or K–12/K–8/K–5/K–3, plus a Morphy Scholastic side event), a fee-ladder timeline with member discount, a schedule check that flags tight turnarounds for G/90+30…

Borrowed from: ChessRoster, Chesstide and onlineregistration.cc (resumable checklist, quick-add section chips, fee tiers, bye rules…

Trade-off: Every step on one page is fast for experienced TDs but less guided than a one-step-at-a-time wizard for a first-time club rep; the schedule check and the dynamic preview image are extra moving parts.

s_Scan-A.text:
What: Desktop review screen for the scanner: scoresheet photo on the left (the move being checked is highlighted on the sheet), a scoresheet-style move list in the centre that labels "fixed automatically" (7.

Borrowed from: Chess67 (photo and moves side by side, threefold-repetition flag, one-tap export), lichess (import for analysis…

Trade-off: Saving and publishing games brings storage, consent and juniors'-privacy rules to a feature that keeps nothing today, and TD mode only works when the pairings live in LCA's system; board is 150px taller than planned.

s_Scan-B.text:
What: Four phones: (1) capture with a gold guide frame that finds the sheet and shoots when steady, plus upload, back side and the daily scan count; (2) reading, with the photo, a reading line, staged progress (grid, handwriting, legality, pairing match) and moves streaming in with "9...?" flagged…

Borrowed from: Chess67 (photo-and-moves scanner with one-tap export), lichess (import for analysis)…

Trade-off: Auto-capture and streamed progress turn today's single request into a camera path plus an async job; checking one flag per screen is slower than editing in a list when a sheet has many flags.

b_start.text: How to use this board: start with the overview and the recommended picks beside it, then flip pages with the page menu. The implementation brief (REDESIGN_SPEC.md) turns the picks into buildable work. Every option has a grey note underneath: What / Borrowed from / Trade-off. Options are built to mix and match, so pick per section, then pick one look. Invented details are badged Sample data; everything else is real LCA data.

b_looks.text: Seven complete looks on the same brand (navy #1a2744 + gold #c8a94a). Top row: style tiles (type, color, components, chess data). Bottom row: the same sample page in each look, so you compare like with like. Gold works as text only on navy (6.5:1); on white it fails (2.3:1), so each look has a darker gold for light grounds.

b_nav.text: Evidence: visible desktop nav beats hidden menus (NN/g: hamburger used 27% of the time vs ~50% for visible links). Audience labels (Parents, Players) work as homepage entry points, not as the main nav (NN/g, GOV.UK). Donate · Log in · Join top-right, same order on every page (WCAG 3.2.6).

b_home.text: A homepage must say who LCA is, give the top 3–4 tasks a clear start, show real dated content, and keep motion minimal (NN/g). The current 5-second slideshow has no pause control, which fails WCAG 2.2.2 (Level A) — all six options replace it.

b_tournaments.text: A dated list beats a month grid for finding dates (Hund et al. 2014). Show applied filters as removable chips with a visible result count; keep filters in the URL (Baymard, NN/g). Mix of LCA-run events and Gulf South partner listings — make the source obvious. Event names and dates here are real, from the live feed.

b_event.text: On phones the Register card currently renders after the entire player list. Recommended mobile order: title → key facts → Register + price → sections & fees → schedule → prizes → entries → venue → rules. Show facts as structure, not shorthand prose (US Chess TLAs are the cautionary tale).

b_register.text: Baymard: forced account creation causes 18% of checkout abandonment (24% in 2022) and surprise costs 40%. GOV.UK: ask eligibility first, end with check-your-answers, confirm with what happens next. One checkout for a whole family is LCA's edge over KingRegistration.

t_live.text: Tournament day — pairings, standings, TV, print

b_live.text: At the venue, players check pairings on phones in a crowd. Find-my-name, my board pinned (and my kids'), 'Updated 2 min ago', bigger text. Real tables with a frozen Player column; results as letter + color. QR codes on the wall replace the print scramble (Chess67's Campbell story).

b_clubs.text: With the map beside the list, 95% of testers used it; on list-only sites 65% never found the map (Baymard). Lead club cards with WHEN they meet. 7 of 25 clubs show no schedule today — a 'last confirmed' stamp and 'report outdated info' keep volunteer listings honest (NC Chess).

b_club.text: For most Louisiana clubs the LCA club page is their only web presence. A first-time visitor needs two answers before anything else: when do you meet, and what happens on my first visit (parkrun, Downriver).

b_scholastic.text: Scholastic families are LCA's biggest group of newcomers — often not chess players, often on phones. Explain jargon inline (G/30+5, section, bye), draw the tournament-day timeline, and say plainly what LCA collects about kids.

b_news.text: Date every item. Rows scan faster than cards for chronological feeds (NN/g). 'From the clubs' is switched off today and Facebook posts are pulled server-side. Results recaps with named winners turn events into community stories.

b_about.text: A volunteer board earns trust by being visibly current: next meeting, minutes, bylaws as web pages (PDF as a download), 'Last updated' stamps, a yearly financial summary. Only 4% of nonprofit sites say where money goes (NN/g).

b_membership.text: LCA tiers depend on who you are (adult, K–12, family, 65+), not on upgrading — so lead with 'Which one fits you?'. Family $25 equals Adult + 2 Scholastic; it only saves money with 3 children. There is no visible Donate entry point on the site today.

b_account.text: Dashboards should show status and the next action at a glance: membership expiry, upcoming entries, payment pending, US Chess expiring before an event (NN/g, Baymard). One login can be member + parent + club rep + TD + board — sections appear by role, no mode switch.

b_workspace.text: Directors work on laptops and tablets at the venue. Today's manage page has 5 tabs and ~11 cards; its tables need 640–840px and scroll sideways on a tablet. Priorities: check-in speed, pairing, results entry, publishing, printing.

b_scanner.text: The scanner is live (photo → moves → lichess). Gaps: nothing is saved, no board while correcting, the photo can't be seen next to the moves. Chess67 now sells a scanner with photo and moves side by side.

b_sources.text: Every source behind this board, grouped: peer federations, tournament platforms, clubs and chess brands, cross-domain sites, evidence (NN/g, Baymard, GOV.UK, USWDS, WCAG 2.2), type and visual references, plus the LCA codebase inventory.
